LESSON: ROTE COUNTING

Grade: PP2
Subject: MATHEMATICS ACTIVITIES
Strand: NUMBERS
Topic 2.1: Rote counting

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Rote counting. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. rote count using actions up to 50 for enhancing acquisition of numeracy
2. enjoy rote counting up to 50 in their daily life. television educational programmes on rote counting. on rote counting with actions.

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. rote count using actions up to 50 for enhancing acquisition of numeracy
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to rote count using actions up to 50 for enhancing acquisition of numeracy. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

2. enjoy rote counting up to 50 in their daily life. television educational programmes on rote counting. on rote counting with actions.
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to enjoy rote counting up to 50 in their daily life. television educational programmes on rote counting. on rote counting with actions. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At the market in your county, count 10 mangoes. Put them in 2 groups of 5. That is sorting and grouping.

Example 2: In class, count the desks in your row. Write the number in figures and in words.

Example 3: If you have 7 shillings and your parent gives you 5 more, you have 12 shillings. That is addition.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Rote counting.
2. Explain Rote counting to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Rote counting.
4. Show that you can: rote count using actions up to 50 for enhancing acquisition of numeracy
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Rote counting. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why is Rote counting important to you?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. rote count using actions up to 50 for enhancing acquisition of numeracy
2. enjoy rote counting up to 50 in their daily life. television educational programmes on rote counting. on rote counting with actions.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Learner lesson
